summary:
Project summary:

 7-Sol Mars Outpost Commander is an interactive 3D space survival simulation designed to help young learners understand the real engineering and environmental challenges of living on Mars. Built in Unity 6 using real NASA open datasets, players manage a Martian base across 7 Sols by balancing a zero-sum 100% power budget across three vital systems: Life Support, Radiation Shielding, and Science/Communications. Every decision involves real trade-offs—boosting shields to survive solar flares reduces power for oxygen and greenhouse food production, while dust storms and a 14-minute Mars-to-Earth signal delay test strategic planning. Featuring Cadet and Commander difficulty modes, tangible 3D visual feedback, and plain-language explanations, the simulation transforms complex space weather and astronaut health data into an engaging hands-on learning experience.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Project GenZentrix (7-Sol Mars Outpost Commander) places players in command of a Martian research outpost for 7 Sols (Martian days). At each Sol, players allocate a fixed 100% power supply across three interdependent systems using zero-sum sliders: Life Support (Oxygen/Food & Greenhouse), Radiation Shielding, and Science/Communications. Increasing power to one system automatically reduces power available to the others, teaching real-world resource trade-offs. Players must respond to dynamic crisis events grounded in NASA space weather and Mars environmental records—such as M-Class Solar Flares, regional dust storms, sub-zero temperatures (-60°C), and a 14-minute Mars-to-Earth communication delay.

Visual Feedback & Accessibility:

The 3D Martian outpost reacts directly to player choices: activating high shielding powers up a visible blue protective dome around the habitat, life support adjustments change greenhouse lighting, and incoming storms trigger a 3D Martian dust storm effect. The game includes two difficulty modes—Cadet Mode for younger students and Commander Mode for older learners—paired with plain-language explanations of space terminology.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

By turning complex space science into an interactive decision-making experience, the project builds systems thinking, STEM curiosity, and data literacy among students without requiring prior technical knowledge.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

Game Engine & Rendering: Unity 6 (Universal Render Pipeline / URP) and WebGL Build Support
Programming & Version Control: C# (OutpostManager simulation logic, zero-sum slider engine, and 3D FX triggers), Visual Studio Code, and Git/GitHub
3D Assets & Integration: NASA 3D Resources (Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover glTF/GLB model via Unity glTFast), Kenney Space Kit, and Unity Terrain & Particle Systems
dataRefs: NASA Mars Rover Photos & Mission Sol API
